title: Algorithms
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Design and analyze algorithms: asymptotic analysis and correctness proofs, recurrences and the master theorem, divide and conquer, sorting and its lower bound, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, graph search, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, network flow, and an introduction to P, NP and NP-completeness.

weeks.4: Sorting algorithms and the comparison lower bound
weeks.6: Dynamic programming I: memoization and tabulation
weeks.7: Dynamic programming II: sequences and knapsack
weeks.8: Graph search: BFS, DFS and topological sort
weeks.9: Shortest paths: Dijkstra's algorithm and Bellman–Ford

blocks.deliverable: Solve six recurrences and prove a loop invariant.
Implement and analyze merge sort and quicksort.
Solve three greedy problems with proofs.
Week 7 midterm; solve two dynamic-programming problems with recurrences.
Implement Dijkstra's algorithm with a heap.
Reduce one problem to another and explain why it matters.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Algorithm design portfolio: for five supplied problems, design an algorithm, prove it correct, analyze its running time, implement it with tests, and compare measured performance with your analysis.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
